title: Setting your hourly rate and minimum charge for Flat-pack and fixture installation
audience: Owners of small Australian flat-pack and fixture installation businesses who need a base rate and a minimum charge before they quote.
learningOutcomes: Separate billable hours from non-billable hours, and calculate the time available to bill
Calculate a base hourly rate from the owner's own costs and income target, then compare it with local evidence
Set a minimum charge for single-item visits, and explain it to a client before the visit

instruction.heading: Factors that move the rate
instruction.body: A rate depends on the range of tasks a client can book in one visit, experience, local competition, licence scope and running costs. Vendor listings for Queensland give handyman hourly rates of $65 to $120 and a half-hour call-out minimum of $80 to $150 (The Quote Yard, 10 May 2026). Airtasker's Australian guide says handymen in most states charge $80 to $300 an hour, but it gives no basis for that range. These are marketplace figures, not regulator data, so use them only as a sense check. The research found no Victorian or NSW price for flat-pack or fixture work.

instruction.heading: Count only the hours that can be billed
instruction.body: Travel, quoting, admin, marketing, training, van and tool upkeep, sick days and leave are not billable. Jobber says billable time typically makes up 60 to 80 per cent of working hours, which is a general range rather than an Australian figure. Log one month of paid and billable time before you choose a figure, because a short-visit business may fall below that range.

instruction.heading: Build the rate from costs and income
instruction.body: Add the annual running costs, including insurance, van, tools, phone, software, marketing and accounting, and the income you need, including on-costs such as leave and superannuation. Business.gov.au says on-costs belong in the hourly figure. Divide the total by billable hours to reach the base rate. Confirm the tax and leave treatment with a registered tax agent before the rate is published.

instruction.heading: Set a minimum charge for single-item visits
instruction.body: A single-item visit, such as one TV mount, still pays for travel, set-up and admin. Vendor figures give a minimum service fee of $80 to $120 for small jobs (Airtasker, Australia, 13 March 2024) and a half-hour call-out minimum of $80 to $150 in Queensland (The Quote Yard). Define what the minimum includes, such as travel within a set area and a set amount of on-site time, and state it before the visit. Do not stack a separate minimum on each item in one visit; price the visit as one labour amount.

instruction.heading: Review the rate
instruction.body: Review the rate about every three months (Business Victoria, undated). Give repeat clients notice of a rise, and honour quotes already approved at the old rate. Keep a dated record of each change and the reason for it.

procedure: Log one month of paid hours and billable hours to find the billable share.
List the annual running costs, including insurance, van, tools, phone, software and marketing.
Add the income you need, including on-costs for leave and superannuation as confirmed by a registered tax agent.
Divide the total by the billable hours to find the base rate.
Set a minimum charge that covers travel, set-up and admin for a single-item visit, and state it in writing.
Review the rate each quarter, and record any change and the reason for it.

workedExamples.situation: Illustrative figures only. An owner has 2,000 paid hours in a year. Of those, 65 per cent are billable (illustrative, within Jobber's 60 to 80 per cent range), which gives 1,300 billable hours. Annual running costs are $30,000 and the income target before tax is $70,000 (both illustrative).
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the base rate, and what minimum should a single TV mount visit carry?
workedExamples.reasoning: The total to recover is $100,000. Divided by 1,300 billable hours, the base rate is $76.92 an hour (illustrative). A single TV mount visit with 30 minutes of travel, 15 minutes of set-up and 15 minutes of admin makes 70 minutes of time, which is $89.74 at the base rate (illustrative arithmetic). The Queensland vendor half-hour call-out range of $80 to $150 and the Airtasker minimum service fee of $80 to $120 both sit around that figure. The owner chooses a minimum, states it before the visit, and does not add a second minimum for another item in the same visit.

commonErrors.error: Setting a rate from a published average or a competitor's figure without checking the costs.
commonErrors.prevention: Build the base rate from the owner's own costs and billable hours, then compare it with local evidence.

commonErrors.error: Pricing as though every paid hour could be billed.
commonErrors.prevention: Subtract the non-billable time before dividing.

commonErrors.error: Taking single-item visits at the same rate, without covering travel and set-up.
commonErrors.prevention: Set and state a minimum charge that covers travel, set-up and admin.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The ACCC says misleading price statements are prohibited, and a single advertised price should include any additional charges. The material read for this variant does not address minimum or call-out charges. Check those points with current ACCC guidance or a legal adviser before you publish a price sheet.
Confirm the tax treatment of leave and superannuation for your own situation with a registered tax agent before the rate is published.

A rate does not authorise electrical, plumbing or other licensed work. Light fittings, power points and cabling are excluded from the rate in this course, and the state rule was not settled by the research. Refer those items to a licensed tradesperson.

qualityStandard: Billable hours are calculated from a logged month, not assumed.
The base rate is built from the owner's costs and income target, and is compared with local evidence.
A minimum charge is set and stated before any single-item visit.
documentationEvidence: Annual costs and income worksheet, with the source and date of each cost
Billable hours calculation showing the non-billable deductions
Price sheet showing the base rate, the minimum charge and the review date
summary: Price from billable hours, not from paid hours.
Build the rate from costs and a stated income target, then check it against local evidence.
Set and state a minimum charge for single-item visits.

knowledgeChecks.question: An owner can bill only some of the paid hours. How should the rate be built?
options: From all paid hours, so the rate looks lower
From billable hours, so the costs and income are covered by the work that can be billed
From the rate the nearest competitor advertises this week
From the rate the owner would like the market to pay

knowledgeChecks.question: Why set a minimum charge for a single-item visit?
options: Because a single item needs no travel or set-up time
Because travel, set-up and admin time does not shrink with the size of the job
Because clients expect every visit to cost the same amount
Because a minimum charge replaces a written quote

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best source for checking a base hourly rate?
options: The rate on the first page of a bidding site this week
A friend's rate, without checking the costs
The owner's own costs and billable hours, compared with local evidence
A single national average with no stated basis

sourceReferences: The Quote Yard, Handyman services QLD, https://www.thequoteyard.com.au/services/handyman-services-qld, published 10 May 2026. Vendor estimates: hourly rate $65 to $120; half-hour call-out minimum $80 to $150.

Airtasker, 'Handyman pricing guide: How much to charge for a job' (AU), https://www.airtasker.com/au/guides/handyman-pricing/, last updated 13 March 2024. Vendor. Minimum service fee $80 to $120; handymen in most states $80 to $300 an hour, with no stated basis.

Jobber Academy, 'What are billable hours', https://getjobber.com/academy/what-are-billable-hours/, published 5 November 2024, last modified 20 July 2026. Billable time typically 60 to 80 per cent of working hours; general range, not Australian.

business.gov.au, 'Choose a pricing strategy', https://business.gov.au/products-and-services/choose-a-pricing-strategy, page metadata dated 1 October 2026. On-costs such as super, leave and tax belong in the hourly figure.

Business Victoria, 'Develop a pricing strategy', https://business.vic.gov.au/business-information/finance/pricing-for-profit/develop-a-pricing-strategy, no date shown. Review prices about every three months.
